site.name: Kinmeet
site.leave: Leave the application (answers won't be kept)

footer.tagline: Free, all-ages park meets for the alterhuman family. Being founded in the open, autumn 2026.
footer.no_tracking: No cookies, no trackers. The only outside script is a spam check on our forms.
footer.fonts: Fonts: {fredoka} and {atkinson}, shared under an open font licence.

hero.title: We're starting Kinmeet. Want to help?
hero.lede: Kinmeet will be free, all-ages meets in parks for the alterhuman family: games, crafts and good company, run by local volunteers. Before the first one, we need a few more people.
hero.art_button: Make us some art! It's a paid role
hero.art_label: A picnic in a park: blankets in an open ring, everyone welcome

roles.title: Roles we're looking for
roles.lede: None of these need experience. Each one comes with a written role description and a handover note.

parents.title: Here as a parent?
parents.body: Our all-ages promise and safeguarding policy are being written now. Our trustees will adopt them before anyone volunteers at a meet, and they'll be public before the first meet.

trustee.title: Trustee
trustee.summary: Hold the keys with us: co-sign for the bank account, vote on big decisions, and say no when something's wrong.

involves.heading: What it involves
involves.body: Trustees hold Kinmeet to account. You'll co-sign for the bank account with one other trustee, vote on the decisions that go in the decisions log, and read the minutes and the accounts with a critical eye. If something's wrong, you're one of the people who can say so and make it stop.

asks.heading: What it asks
asks.body: An evening a month for a video meeting. Replying to messages within a week. Reading the minutes and the accounts when they're published.

gets.heading: What you get
gets.body: A say in how Kinmeet works from the very beginning, a written role description and a handover note, and a first meeting with the agenda already written.

good_to_know.heading: Good to know
good_to_know.body: We're registering Kinmeet as a charity (a CIO) straight away. We'll ask the Charity Commission to keep trustees' names off its public register, but it only agrees where there's evidence of risk. If it says no, your legal name will be on the register. That's the one place it would appear, and we'll talk it through before you commit. If you'd personally be at risk, you can ask for your own name to be withheld too, and we'll help with that.

time.label: Time
time.value: An evening a month, plus replies within a week

checks.label: Checks
checks.value: A basic DBS (criminal record) check, which we arrange and pay for, or enhanced if our checking body confirms the role is eligible

you_need.label: You need to be
you_need.value: 18 or over, and not related to, in a relationship with, or living with anyone already on the founding team

reply.title: We reply within seven days
reply.body: Even if it's to say we need a bit longer.

chat.title: A 30-minute chat
chat.body: On video or in a café, your choice. Bring questions; it's for you too.

references.title: References, then we decide
references.body: We ask two people who know you for a short reference. If it's a no, we tell you why.

yes.title: If it's a yes
yes.body: A basic DBS check, which we arrange and pay for, a handover pack, and your appointment recorded in the minutes by role title.

note.heading: About the DBS check
note.body: This role needs a basic DBS check, which we arrange and pay for. If our checking body confirms the role is eligible for an enhanced check, we'll arrange that instead. Something on your record doesn't automatically rule you out; we'd talk it through in confidence. We never keep a copy of the certificate, only that we saw it, the date and the outcome.

connection_to_founders.label: Are you connected to anyone already on the founding team?
connection_to_founders.hint: Trustees, including the treasurer and safeguarding lead, need to be independent of each other. Roles that aren't trustee roles, like the artists and pilot group leads, don't have this rule.

choices.related_or_household: Yes: we're related, in a relationship, or live together
choices.friend_or_acquaintance: Yes: we're friends, or know each other

notes.friend_or_acquaintance: That's fine. Trustees who know each other say so to the rest of the board, and step out of any decision where it could matter.
notes.not_sure: That's fine. Carry on, and we'll talk it through when we chat.

trustee_rules_confirmed.label: I've read the Charity Commission's rules on who can't be a trustee, and as far as I know none apply to me.
trustee_rules_confirmed.link: Read the rules on GOV.UK (opens in a new tab)

why_trustee.label: Why would you like to be a trustee?
why_trustee.hint: A few sentences is plenty. There's no right answer.

experience.label: Anything you've done that feels relevant? (optional)
experience.hint: Committees, clubs, looking after money, moderating a server. Nothing is fine too.

artist-mark.title: Artist: the mark
artist-mark.summary: Draw our open-ring logo: leaves, stones and prints in a circle, with a gap for the door.

artist-illustration.title: Artist: illustration
artist-illustration.summary: The picnic scene on the front page, and a set of small spot drawings to go with it.

safeguarding-lead.title: Safeguarding lead
safeguarding-lead.summary: The person anyone can turn to with a worry about someone's safety, including young people themselves. Trained before your first case, with a deputy to share the load.

tags.time: On call for concerns, with a deputy

treasurer.title: Treasurer
treasurer.summary: Keep the accounts, and publish a money summary by category every quarter, so anyone can see where it goes.

pilot-group-lead.title: Pilot group lead
pilot-group-lead.summary: Run one of our first meets near you, with friends if you've got them. We haven't picked any places yet: tell us where you are and we'll choose from who applies.

apply.intro: Four short steps, about five minutes. Your answers stay in this browser tab until you send them.
apply.time_note: About five minutes. Your answers stay in this browser tab until you send them.

callName.label: What should we call you?
callName.hint: Your name or your community name. This is what we'll use.

email.label: Email address
email.hint: We'll only use it to reply about your application.

where_it_goes.heading: Where this goes
where_it_goes.body: Your application is stored securely by Kinmeet, and only the founder reads it. If you're not appointed, we delete it 6 months after we tell you. If you are, it becomes part of your trustee record. The privacy notice has the details.

apply.noscript: This form needs JavaScript to work. Please turn it on, or come back in a browser that has it.

under_18.title: These roles need an adult
under_18.body: Thanks for wanting to help. Every one of these roles involves checks, money or responsibility, so they're for people aged 18 or over.
under_18.next: When meets start, all-ages is the whole point, and you'd be very welcome. If you're under 16, come along with a parent or carer. If you're 16 or 17, you can come on your own once a parent or carer has said yes.

not_independent.title: Trustees need to be independent
not_independent.body: Thanks for wanting to help. Trustees hold each other to account, so a trustee can't be related to, in a relationship with, or living with anyone else on the founding team.
not_independent.next: Roles that aren't trustee roles, like the artists and pilot group leads, don't have this rule, so have a look at those.

kept.heading: What happens to your message
kept.body: Your message is stored securely by Kinmeet. We delete it automatically 12 months after our last reply to you, or 12 months after you sent it if we haven't replied.
kept.safety: If your message tells us someone may be at risk, we pass it to our safeguarding lead, who keeps it securely and separately. If someone needs protecting, they may share it with services that can help, such as the police.

danger.heading: If someone is in danger
danger.body: Call 999 straight away. Messages here aren't read around the clock.

privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.intro: Kinmeet is being set up as a charity for the alterhuman community. We collect as little about you as we can, we never track you, and we never sell or share your details for marketing.

controller.heading: Who is responsible for your data
controller.not_yet: Kinmeet is not yet a registered charity. Until it is, the person responsible for your data is Kinmeet's founder.
controller.cio: When Kinmeet becomes a charity (a CIO), it will take over responsibility and we will update this page.

collect.heading: What we collect
collect.hello_label: If you use the say hello form:
collect.hello: {label} the name you choose to give us (a community name is fine), your email address and your message.
collect.trustee_label: If you apply to be a founding trustee:
collect.trustee: {label} your community name, your contact details and your answers on the form. We only ask for your legal name and other details if we offer you a place.
collect.form: {label} Cloudflare Turnstile checks that you are a person, not a bot. It runs only on pages with forms.

never.heading: What we never collect
never.analytics: No analytics or tracking of any kind, and no advertising.
never.cookies: No tracking cookies. Any cookie used by us or by Turnstile is only there to make the site or a form work.
never.ip: No record of your IP address with anything you send us.
never.other_sites: Nothing from other websites: our pages load only from our own site, apart from Turnstile on form pages.

hello.basis: Our legitimate interest in answering people who contact us

trustee.basis: Our legitimate interest in setting up the charity safely

turnstile.why: To stop spam and abuse of our forms
turnstile.basis: Our legitimate interest in keeping the forms safe

others.heading: Who else sees it
others.body: Only {cloudflare}, which hosts our website and stores our data for us under a contract, and runs Turnstile. Cloudflare is not allowed to use your data for anything else. We keep our data in Europe where Cloudflare lets us choose. Nobody else sees your details unless the law requires it, or someone is at risk of harm.

keep.heading: How long we keep it
keep.hello: Say hello messages: 12 months after our last reply.
keep.trustee: Trustee applications that are not taken forward: 6 months after we tell you.
keep.trustee_record: If you become a trustee, your application becomes part of your trustee record, which we explain to you at the time.

rights.heading: Your rights
rights.ask: You can ask us for a copy of what we hold about you, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it. You can also object to how we use it.
rights.email: Email {address} and we will reply within one month. It is free.
rights.complain: If you are unhappy with how we handle your data, please tell us first. You can also complain to the Information Commissioner's Office at ico.org.uk or on 0303 123 1113.

under_18.heading: If you are under 18
under_18.rights: You have the same rights as everyone else. You do not need a parent's permission to write to us.
under_18.private: Please do not send us anything private about yourself or anyone else in a message.

changes.heading: Changes
changes.body: We will update this page when Kinmeet becomes a charity and when we add new features, and show the date at the top.

draft.scrambled_ip: To stop spam, our website briefly uses a scrambled version of your internet connection's address (IP address) to limit how many forms can be sent from one place in a minute. It is never saved with what you send and is forgotten within minutes.
draft.backups: After deletion, a copy may stay in our secure recovery backups for up to 7 days before it is gone for good.
